caveats: Two gaps left open by topo-clean (6.52 sq km between Muharraq and the mainland, 7.71 sq km in the Capital area) are lagoons/sea channels confirmed by satellite imagery and left out of every admin unit, consistent with the prior boundaries. Edge-matching against the outdated prior (UNHCR-era) admin0 reference would have dropped 16 blocks and severely clipped 29 more, all in land reclaimed since that reference was captured (Diyar Al Muharraq, Amwaj, Durrat Al Bahrain, Sharq Al Hidd, Sharq Sitra City, Um Albaidh, Madinat Salman, Alwajeha Albahriya, Nurana), a 140 sq km (15.6%) loss. This release codes and names the full topology-cleaned geometry instead of edge-matching to the outdated reference; edge-matching can be revisited once an updated admin0 outline is available.
dataset_source: Bahrain Ministry of Municipalities Affairs & Urban Planning
license_title: Creative Commons Attribution for Intergovernmental Organisations (CC BY-IGO)
methodology_other:
Dataset: Built from Bahrain MMA's block-level (admin3) layer, the deepest and most complete of the three supplied levels, with area (admin2) and governorate (admin1) built up from it via schema-join. Topology gaps were filled except for two confirmed water bodies left open. Edge-matching to the outdated prior country outline was skipped because it would have dropped reclaimed-land units; this release packages the full topology-cleaned, coded and name-reviewed geometry instead.  
  
P-codes: Bahrain Ministry of Municipalities Affairs & Urban Planning's own governorate and block codes, embedded inside a hierarchical code prefixed with the ISO2 country code (BH); the area (admin2) level has no source code and is numbered sequentially under its governorate.
name: cod-ab-bhr
notes:
Bahrain administrative level 0-3 boundaries (COD-AB) dataset version 01.  
  
This dataset is structured into 3 levels:  
- Admin 1: 4 Governorate  
- Admin 2: 180 Area  
- Admin 3: 499 Block  
  
  
Note: Base layer is the block level (admin3, 499 units, source columns blockno/bltext), with area (admin2, 180 units) and governorate (admin1, 4 units) built up via schema-join; root code is ISO2 'BH'. admin2 (area) has no source code of its own; codes for all three levels are generated in stage 4 (code-create). admin3 has no source name of its own; the block number (bltext) is used as its name. topo-tools schema-join 0.17.0 silently dropped admin2's own name columns when joining admin3 against an admin2 file already enriched with admin1 columns, because 5 of 180 area names repeat under two different governorates; admin2_name/admin2_name1 were restored manually via a largest-overlap DuckDB join.   
  
  
Dates associated with this dataset:  
- 16 November 2026: dataset reviewed for accuracy and completeness  
- 16 November 2026: valid for use by the humanitarian community  
  
Quality assured, configured, and published by [OCHA Field Information Services (FIS)](https://data.humdata.org/organization/ocha-fiss) and [HDX](https://data.humdata.org/organization/hdx).  
  
Part of the dataset: [Global Subnational Administrative Boundaries](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/cod-ab-global)
